business_scope.primary_industry_name: Foreign Market Feasibility Study and Regulatory Licensing Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Kingdom of Spain; unitary national jurisdiction without sub-state company registration distinction for SL entities)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental European notarial system; statutory framework under the Constitution of 1978)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-Mexico BIT (1995; in force, as amended by Protocol of 2006)
EU-Chile Advanced Framework Agreement (2023; provisional application)
Spain-United States Estate, Inheritance and Gift Tax Treaty (1990; in force; no general income tax treaty currently in force with the United States)
OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) as applied to Spanish double taxation agreements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento del Registro Central de Titularidades Reales; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC); transposition of Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5th AML Directive).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each founding shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular section or competent public authority of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the origin jurisdiction is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to the Spanish incorporation agent (poder para la constitución de la sociedad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille followed by sworn translation into Spanish (traducción jurada)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (when a corporate shareholder is identified as UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company/commercial registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization according to the practice of the originating registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of funds for the statutory capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution in the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization when required by the Spanish notary or receiving Spanish bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and verification of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against PEP databases under art. 14 Ley 10/2010; mandatory screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions (including 1267/1988 ISIL/Al-Qaida), and the national Spanish list maintained by the Secretaría General del Tesoro; practical secondary screening against the OFAC SDN List is required because USD-denominated B2B transfers through correspondent banks will be filtered; any PEP match or sanctions positive triggers enhanced due diligence and senior management approval prior to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central telematic request service via the CIRCE/online registry platform (www.registradores.org); issuance of the official negative denomination certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate denomination must be expressed in the Spanish alphabet script; foreign-language names are admissible only when transliterated into Spanish characters, do not contravene public order or morality, and do not mislead third parties (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, arts. 404-407); the statutory suffix 'S.L.' or the phrase 'Sociedad Limitada' is mandatory; names identical or confusingly similar to an existing Spanish entity are prohibited under LSC art. 347.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco de España (reserved term requiring Bank of Spain authorization)
Ministerio, Gobierno, Estado (terms implying official character are prohibited unless authorized)
Entidad de Dinero Electrónico, Financiera (require Bank of Spain authorization)
Holding, Grupo (admissible only when the entity genuinely controls or belongs to an authorized group)
Names contrary to law, morality or public order (art. 407 RRM)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension exists. If the incorporation deed (escritura de constitución) is not executed within the six-month outer validity limit of the negative certificate under LSC art. 347.2, a fresh certificate must be obtained. Upon rejection, the applicant shall: (i) submit a new online request with an alternative denomination; (ii) file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of the negative resolution; and (iii) if the alzada is dismissed, pursue judicial review before the Audiencia Nacional within the applicable statutory deadlines.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual and serviced-office addresses are generally accepted by Spanish registries for this low-risk consulting industry provided a Spanish correspondence point and administrative service contract are in place; however, a true mail-only virtual address materially increases corporate tax-residency and commercial substance challenge risk before the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT). Best practice is a contracted serviced office with meeting room and documentation facilities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for unannounced physical inspections, quantified at approximately 5% annualized for non-licensed consultancy activities; likelihood materially rises to roughly 20-35% if the entity claims significant VAT credits on intra-EU invoices, applies reduced treaty withholding benefits, or is drawn into a general AEAT inspection program.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative denomination certificate issuance (certificación negativa de denominación social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Colegio de Registradores
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff for telematic issuance, approximately EUR 30, exclusive of lawyer handling fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the incorporation deed (escritura de constitución)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff schedule under Real Decreto 1426/1989; standard SL deed with one to two shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry inscription fee (inscripción en el Registro Mercantil provincial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed registry fee based on share capital, approximately EUR 120

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF provisional) issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Gratuitous statutory issuance; onerous processing only if delegated to a gestoría or legal agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Minimum share capital deposit in blocked Spanish bank account (EUR 3,000 statutory minimum)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish credit institution (CaixaBank, Santander or BBVA) holding the block certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory capital requirement under LSC art. 4; refundable to the company after registry inscription, not a fiscal charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation into Spanish (traducción jurada) of foreign corporate and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traductor jurado) appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, EU and Cooperation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional tariff of sworn translators, approximately EUR 0.15 to 0.25 per word or per-document fixed fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostilles and/or consular legalization of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent origin authority (Secretary of State or consular officer under the Hague Apostille Convention)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille fee of EUR 20-40, assuming three documents; consular legalization fees are higher where applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC file, PEP/sanctions screening and UBO register representation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish AML compliance counsel or colegiada gestoría
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee for Ley 10/2010 CDD file preparation and Registro de Titularidades Reales filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate incorporation counsel, model statute drafting and post-filing registrations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SL incorporation with model statutes, corporate resolutions and registry follow-up

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of Spanish corporate bank account and facility fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-practice account opening and first-year maintenance fee; frequently waived during promotional campaigns

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 20-22 (corporate name), 59-64 (incorporation formalities), 72-89 (registered office), 190-212 (administration and boards) and 275-278 (shareholder resolutions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for the name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial for corporate inscription; authorised notary (Notaría) for execution of the public deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) filed with the Provincial Mercantile Registry, together with Form 036 filed with the Spanish Tax Administration Agency (AEAT).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SL requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation. The capital may be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate issued by a Spanish credit institution in the company's name or by non-cash contributions. No escrow account is legally mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF SOCIEDAD DE RESPONSABILIDAD LIMITADA ADOPTED BY THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS ON [DATE]. After considering the incorporation deed, the board resolves: (1) Each founding shareholder subscribes and fully pays in the shares allocated in the deed, totalling EUR 3,000.00, and capital is declared; (2) The registered office is established at [address], Spain, and the board authorises its inscription in the Mercantile Registry; (3) [Full name] is appointed sole administrator / managing director (Administrador Único / Consejero Delegado) with all statutory powers; (4) Any of the administrator(s) is authorised to execute all public and private documents and to apply for the provisional tax identification number before the Spanish tax administration. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the negative corporate name certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (online via the College of Registrars of Spain)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for a negative name certificate (Certificación negativa de denominación social) to the Registro Mercantil Central, electronically or through any provincial registry. The proposed name must not be identical or unduly similar to any existing Spanish company name. The certificate once issued is valid for three months.
required_dossiers: Name certificate application form
Proposed company name
Applicant's identity document (NIE or passport)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is refused, select a different name and resubmit; if refusal is based on similarity to an existing name, obtain written consent from the conflicting company or provide a supporting legal opinion showing lack of similarity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a provisional bank account and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (bank or savings bank) with a branch in Spain
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the company being formed and deposit the minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, or obtain a certificate of deposit from the bank. The bank must issue a capital deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) to be attached to the notarial deed. The funds are blocked until the deed is registered with the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Draft public deed (borrador de la escritura)
Passports or NIE cards of all founding shareholders
Negative name certificate
If a shareholder is a legal entity, its incorporation certificate and representative's appointment
Anti-money laundering compliance declaration completed by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses due to incomplete KYC documentation, cure by providing the compliance declaration and the name certificate; if refusal is based on non-residence, appoint a Spanish tax or statutory representative to complete the banking verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the public incorporation deed before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Spanish notary bringing the name certificate, bank capital deposit certificate, draft bylaws (estatutos), identity documents, and if applicable powers of attorney. The notary verifies the legal capacity and consent of the incorporators and authorises the public deed. The deed must contain the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, share distribution, administration structure, and the appointment of directors.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Bank capital deposit certificate
Bylaws (estatutos sociales)
Identity documents of all incorporators (NIE or passport)
Notarised power of attorney if any founder acts through a representative
Documentation evidencing the capacity of any corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises defects in the deed or bylaws, amend the draft deed and reschedule the notarial appointment; if a shareholder's legal capacity is questioned, supply the required entity documentation and execute again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the provisional company tax identification number (NIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT) - local tax office or central office for large taxpayers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the deed is executed, submit Form 036 to the AEAT applying for the provisional NIF. Attach a copy of the notarial deed and the directors' and shareholders' tax identifications. The AEAT will issue a provisional NIF valid for six months, pending registration in the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Form 036 (modelo 036) duly signed
Copy of the first copy of the public deed
Tax identification numbers of directors and shareholders
Passport or NIE of the legal representative applying for the NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT queries the application, correct any omissions in Form 036 and resubmit with the complete deed; for non-resident shareholders, ensure a fiscal representative (representante fiscal) is appointed and documented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) corresponding to the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original public deed with the Provincial Mercantile Registry within one month after notarisation. The Registrar examines the legality of the deed and bylaws. If approved, the company is inscribed and acquires legal personality as of the date of registration. After registration, request a certificate of inscription (certificación del registro) for subsequent formalities.
required_dossiers: Original first copy of the public deed
Simple or digital copy of the deed for the registry
Payment receipt for notarial and registry fees
Modelo 600 if capital transfer tax is applicable (usually exempt for company formation under EU law)
Power of attorney if a legal representative is filing on behalf of the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar suspends or refuses the inscription, amend the deed or bylaws as required and resubmit; the suspension notice will specify the defects. If the refusal is unjustified, file an appeal with the Registry Directorate General (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública) within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF, Social Security registration and municipal operating licences
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT; Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social; municipal council (Ayuntamiento)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Mercantile Registry inscription, submit Form 036 again along with the registry certificate to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF. Register the company and, if employees will be hired, the employer code with Social Security. Apply for the municipal activity and opening licence for the physical office, or file a prior communication (comunicación previa) where the activity is exempt. Complete the bank release of the blocked capital by presenting the registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Mercantile Registry inscription
Form 036 for definitive NIF
Lease agreement or title deed for the registered office
Fire safety compliance certificate if required
Identity documents of the legal representative
Municipal licencing application or communication form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT refuses to convert the NIF, obtain a corrected registry certificate and resubmit; if the municipal authority requires a technical project, commission a competent architect to submit a project and obtain the necessary approvals. Delay remedies include filing an appeal or authorisation under the local administrative procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Tourism (General State Administration); however, for a professional consultancy office the local licensing authority is the municipal department of economic activities (Ayuntamiento), and where applicable the Autonomous Community's industry directorate.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Activity Licence (Licencia de Actividad) and Opening Licence (Licencia de Apertura); for office premises below the classified-threshold, a Comunicación Previa de Inicio de Actividad may be sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (MITECO) and the Autonomous Community environmental agency (e.g., Consejería de Transición Ecológica)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III - environmental registration only; the office-based market-entry consultancy activity is generally not subject to a full EIA report unless the premises exceed energy or waste thresholds in the applicable regional environmental ordinance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to municipal sewers must comply with Royal Decree 817/2015 and local sewerage ordinances; VOC emissions from office operations are negligible, but emergency generators or HVAC equipment must meet emission limits under Royal Decree 1027/2007. Waste management must comply with Law 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils, including selective collection and proper record-keeping.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupying the premises, obtain a fire safety certificate in accordance with Regulation for Fire Safety Installations RD 2267/2004 or the fire-safety document of the Technical Building Code, issue a structural load certificate for the office floor from a competent architect, and carry out the workplace health and safety risk assessment and prevention plan required by Law 31/1995.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica – sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish S.L.: apply to AEAT for a provisional NIF before company registration in the Mercantile Registry using Form 036; after registration, obtain the definitive NIF and update the Form 036 record. For a foreign entity: file Form 036, appoint a fiscal representative in Spain, and obtain an NIF or, where taxable supplies are made, a Spanish VAT identification number (NIF-ES) before commencing any taxable activity. Inbound non-resident service providers without a permanent establishment generally require a Spanish NIF solely for tax identity and controlled VAT refund procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – an S.L. is a Spanish resident company subject to corporation tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on worldwide income at a headline 25% rate, with a reduced 15% rate for newly created SMEs meeting statutory thresholds in their first two profit-making years. Foreign non-resident companies without a Spanish permanent establishment remain within Territorial_Scope and are taxed only on Spanish-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spanish law does not offer U.S.-style check-the-box elections; an S.L. is compulsorily taxed at entity level. Available elections include group consolidation (régimen de consolidación fiscal) for tax groups. Under ATAD II domestic anti-hybrid rules, taxpayers must disclose and eliminate hybrid mismatch outcomes; no elective neutralisation is permitted for ordinary S.L. structures. Branches/permanent establishments of foreign companies are taxed on their attributable Spanish-source profits without a transparent pass-through election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold; every business carrying out taxable supplies in Spain must register for VAT before commencing activity, regardless of turnover. Small businesses use ordinary VAT registration and reporting; no general small-trader exemption is available in the Spanish VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Ley 28/2022 (Crea y Crece) and Royal Decree 1007/2023 will make B2B e-invoicing mandatory, with full application now deferred to 30 June 2026 under the EU-wide extension. All taxpayers issuing invoices must comply with the anti-fraud obligations of Ley 11/2021: through certified billing software connected to AEAT's Veri*FACTU system, generating integrity hashes and QR-capable codes, unless the taxpayer is covered by the SII real-time regime. Large enterprises (VAT turnover exceeding €6,000,000) and VAT groups must submit invoice data in near real-time through SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) via web services/API within four calendar days. Electronic invoices in Facturae format are the primary clearance mechanism for B2B cross-border and SII taxpayers. Digital stamping and reporting obligations are satisfied through AEAT's approved software/API integration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to third countries are zero-rated under Art. 21 of the Spanish VAT Law (Ley 37/1992). B2B services provided to a customer established in a third country, including overseas market-entry consultancy, are outside the Spanish VAT scope / effectively zero-rated under Art. 69.1.1°(regla general) and Art. 70 LIVA, provided the recipient is a business established outside the EU, the service is performed from Spain, the invoice records 'IVA 0% exenta – Art. 69 LIVA', and the provider retains evidence of the customer's entrepreneur status, third-country residence, and actual supply. For clients established in another EU Member State, the B2B services are taxed by reverse charge in the client's country and are not subject to Spanish VAT; this is not classed as export zero-rating for Spanish purposes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) validated by Agencia Tributaria's customs electronic system
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document evidencing physical departure from the EU
Bank SWIFT confirmation / inward remittance certificate or other export payment proof
Proof of customer's business status and third-country residence (foreign VAT ID or equivalent registration certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may retrospectively claw back improperly claimed zero-rating, assessing the uncollected Spanish VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and penalty charges under Ley 58/2003. Infractions for omitted VAT typically attract penalties ranging from 50% to 150% of the disguised VAT amount; material misstatements require submission of corrective self-invoice. Where the fraudulent or fictitious export results in unpaid VAT exceeding €120,000, criminal tax fraud liability arises under Art. 305 of the Criminal Code (punishable by imprisonment and fines). All export substantiation files must be retained for at least five years from the reporting period and be available for AEAT inspection on demand.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), complemented by the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOMINV) of the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, which administers the foreign investment and capital-movement liberalisation regime under Law 19/2003; Spain maintains no separate foreign exchange control permit authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates full euro convertibility on both current and capital account under Articles 63–66 TFEU, Law 19/2003 and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Freely convertible and unrestricted: receipt of export fees, equity capital injections, shareholder loans, dividend remittances and management-service payments. No Central Bank prior approval, no convertibility tax (IETM does not apply) and no split-rating limitation exist. The only tangible hurdles for profit remittance to non-resident shareholders are (i) Spanish non-resident income tax (IRNR) withholding at 19% internal or a treaty-reduced rate under Spain–LatAm DTTs (typically 5–10% for dividends under the Mexico, Chile, Peru and Uruguay treaties), and (ii) statistical declaration duties to Banco de España via Form D-1/D-2 for any single operation reaching EUR 50,000 or annual aggregate above EUR 1,000,000. For the ES_SL advisory business, credibility friction remains only when the counterpart remitting jurisdiction (e.g., Argentina, Cuba, Venezuela) imposes its own FX controls; inbound funds must then be channelled through a neutral correspondent hub and the SL must document the origin chain to avoid bank-side source-of-funds rejection.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of exported advisory service proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio. The SL may lawfully retain EUR-denominated and foreign-currency receipts (USD, MXN, BRL, CLP) in domestic divisa accounts or in EEA credit institutions without forced sale. The only binding duty is statistical: Banco de España Circular 1/2022 requires the SL to file Form D-1 within the month after the transaction for any export or service receipt equal to or above EUR 50,000 per operation (EUR 1,000,000 cumulative 12-month threshold triggers aggregate reporting even when individual operations are below the single threshold). The compliance file for each receipt must pair the commercial invoice, the SWIFT MT103 credit advice, the underlying market-entry advisory contract, and — when the payer is a related party — an arm's-length transfer-pricing documentation set per OECD Chapter VI.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operational Account (Cuenta Operativa) with attached divisa sub-accounts (USD, MXN) and an international corporate banking desk for LatAm receipts and correspondent routing
Operational Treasury Account plus inward capital-receipt verification cell used to evidence shareholder equity injections
Corporate Operational Account and auxiliary foreign-currency collection account for non-EUR service fees
Operational Account with dedicated LatAm correspondent clearing through Banco Sabadell's Miami and Mexico connectivity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for ancillary operational B2B disbursement rails (Wise B2B, Revolut Business and Qonto passported into Spain under PSD2 without a separate Spanish e-money licence); Medium-to-Low as the sole treasury bank of the ES_SL. Legal and practical constraints: (i) EMIs may not carry out lending activities, therefore no overdraft or credit-line facility and no capital-escrow verification role; (ii) EMI balances are safeguarded under e-money rules, not insured by the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGD); (iii) only credit institutions can issue the corporate banking certificates and detailed BOP classifications that Banco de España expects for D-1/D-2 reconciliation; (iv) an EMI providing services in Spain under passporting must register its activity profile with Banco de España and the counterparty relationship remains supervised by the home-state regulator; (v) Wise's B2B rail is ideal for sub-EUR 50,000 fast FX settlements but must be mirrored to a Santander or Sabadell account for operative treasury, Modelo 216 withholding documentation and any line of credit. Feasibility rating: High as a secondary clearing edge; Low as the primary account-holding institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto standard at Tier-1 Spanish banks is a physical interview of at least one joint administrator (administrador mancomunado) or a formally appointed attorney holding a Spanish notarised power of attorney; fully remote opening is legally available under Real Decreto-ley 7/2021 video-identification rules, but for a foreign-owned SL in a Low_Risk_Standard service scope the banks apply a risk-based first-person rule that can extend onboarding to 3–4 weeks. Practical recommendation: execute one single visit to Madrid or Barcelona — the appointed director attends a corporate welcome-desk interview at the chosen branch, signs the account opening minutes (acta), presents the passport, NIF certificate, commercial registry deed and UBO declaration; onboarding then completes in 5–10 banking days and the bank compiles the full statutory KYC file. Alternative remote path: grant via Spanish notary a durable power (poder preventivo) to a local gestor and open through digital-facilitator banks (Banca March, EVO Banco, OpenBank) which accept simplified video onboarding; nevertheless, for capital receipts, divisa sub-accounts and Banco de España-facing declarations, a full-service relationship with Santander, BBVA or CaixaBank is the advised stable core.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity — the ES_SL shows two or more layers of intermediate holding vehicles, or a LatAm corporate shareholder lacks a PEP and sanctions status certificate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full Declaración de Titular Real (beneficial-owner declaration) executed by all shareholders; Registro Mercantil Central certification issued within the last 30 days and notarised; clear shareholding organigram ending at natural persons; apostilled certificates of good standing and constitutive deeds for each chain entity with Spanish notarised translation; bank-reference letters from every underlying entity; and the Spanish Beneficial Ownership Registry (RLS) filing receipt required by art. 26 of Law 10/2010.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds scrutiny on the inbound equity capital injection arriving from a non-EEA jurisdiction with domestic FX controls or elevated sanctions exposure (e.g., Venezuela, Cuba, Iran-linked funds routed via Mexico).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 chain with correspondent leg visible; source-of-funds affidavit issued by the remitting bank (apostilled and Spanish-translated); prior three-year tax returns of the contributing shareholder; executed invoice or contract evidencing the commercial origin of the wealth; for contributions above EUR 100,000, the Banco de España D-1 declaration and a look-through legal opinion prepared by Spanish counsel grounding the transaction in Law 19/2003 art. 2; all counterparties certified as free of EU restrictive measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Activity-substance mismatch — the declared ISIC 7020 consultancy receives fees from foreign counterparties before any Spanish payroll, rent or VAT evidence appears on file.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed market-entry advisory agreement; dated deliverables (feasibility study, regulatory licensing work-plan, market-entry roadmap); batch of invoices matched to the VAT quarterly return (Modelo 303) and paid via SWIFT/SEPA; Spanish-resident sub-consultancy contracts; office lease or co-working service agreement; travel and tele-presence records proving physical work performed; management letter confirming that the SL is not a passive shell.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP exposure — any director or UBO has recently held public office in a LatAm jurisdiction (former trade commissioner, customs director, minister), triggering mandatory enhanced due diligence and a possible 90-day hold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-declaration; negative PEP certificate from the origin jurisdiction (apostilled); professional biography and post-office gap analysis; wealth-origin statement covering salary, pension and divestment proceeds; notarised board resolution confirming functional independence; and a certificate of no criminal record (certificado de antecedentes penales) from the UBO's country of nationality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: US/FATCA fingerprint — any UBO holds a US passport or green card, which activates FATCA/CRS enhanced review and, in some banks, transfer restrictions on mixed-country directorships.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: W-8BEN-E or W-9 (as applicable) for each US-linked person; CRS self-certification of the SL and each UBO using the bank's standard tax-residence declaration; proof of primary residence (US tax filing record plus state ID); a counsel letter confirming that the SL has no US FDAP or withholdable payment stream; and negative OFAC and political-exposure screening results.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital subscriptions (suscripción or aumento de capital) and shareholder loans from non-resident owners are executed by SWIFT MT103 through EU, US, or LatAm correspondent banks into the SL's Spanish account; EUR legs settle final on TARGET2 and USD legs via euro-correspondent clearing. The receiving bank labels the instruction with ECB Balance-of-Payments category K/6 (capital for business operations) or the equivalent Banco de España D-1 code, and the remittance info must state the corporate purpose code in the exact form:
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EUR-denominated supplier, payroll and sub-advisor settlements across the EEA — final irrevocation on TARGET2 within seconds and ISO 20022 pain.001 messaging; (ii) SWIFT MT103 / MT103+ with SWIFT GPI for USD, MXN, BRL, CLP and COP fee payments to LatAm regulatory agencies, law firms and market-entry partners, enabling D+0/D+1 delivery and full-track tracing; (iii) commercial documentary Letters of Credit (UCP600) remain available but are structurally redundant for pure ISIC 7020 consultancy and are recommended only when a market-entry bundle also includes hardware or software licensing. Every outbound disbursement must pass three controls simultaneously: the Spanish IRNR withholding regime (Modelo 216 filing in the same quarter, 19% or treaty-reduced when the non-resident recipient holds a residency certificate); the Banco de España D-2 monthly declaration for cumulative payments above EUR 50,000 per operation or EUR 1,000,000 annual; and, for related-party LatAm recipients, an arm's-length transfer-pricing memo within the tax file. Weekly matching policy: receive in USD or MXN on the divisa sub-account, convert at the recommended daily fixing or under a hedged forward, settle EUR obligations via SEPA; Wise B2B serves as a fallback rail for sub-EUR 50,000 legs and the balance is swept end-of-day to the main Santander or Sabadell account for full audit transparency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL, EUR/CLP) contracted under an ISDA Master with a Spanish credit institution or EU investment firm — permitted solely for hedging identifiable export-receipt exposure, documented against an underlying invoice, purchase order or board-approved cash-flow schedule.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on restricted-frequency LatAm currencies (notably ARS/USD, USD/PEN, USD/UYU) — permitted when executed by an authorised counterparty with EUR or USD cash settlement based on a published fixing, provided the notional corresponds to a permitted commercial obligation of the SL and the hedging purpose is evidenced.

Cross-currency swaps and FX-swap rollovers for structurally matching multi-month USD/MXN receivables against EUR payables — permitted under the MiFID II hedging exemption when the SL is classified as an elective professional or eligible counterparty, subject to EMIR trade reporting and no central clearing obligation below the clearing threshold.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts, including the beneficial ownership declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors must prepare accounts within three months after financial year-end; shareholders must approve them within six months; filing is due within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, filing is generally due by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may occur if accounts remain unfiled for one year after the filing deadline. ICAC may impose statutory fines, generally EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher limits for qualifying larger groups. Spain does not generally apply automatic administrative strike-off solely for late annual accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of accounting books and corporate minute books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronic legalization is generally due within four months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, the standard deadline is 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted legalization may impair evidentiary value, cause compliance deficiencies, and trigger registry or audit observations. No standard automatic strike-off applies solely for late book legalization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, Modelo 200
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year; for a 31 December year-end, normally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties, late-payment interest, and collection surcharges may apply. Penalties depend on whether tax is payable, whether filing is voluntary, and whether the tax authority has issued a prior request.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership information confirmation and update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and Central Registry of Beneficial Ownership, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Beneficial ownership information must be reported with the annual accounts and updated promptly when ownership, control, or identifying information changes. The annual accounts filing cycle is generally completed by the end of July for a 31 December year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or missing beneficial ownership information may result in registry rejection, inability to obtain a beneficial ownership certificate, AML escalation, and regulatory or administrative sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average annual employees of 50. Audits are also mandatory for certain regulated, public-interest, group, securities, and other legally specified entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the Spanish General Accounting Plan. IFRS is generally mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply to other consolidated groups under applicable Spanish rules; it is not the ordinary framework for standalone SL accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain current beneficial ownership information, identify the natural persons ultimately owning or controlling the company, report the beneficial ownership declaration with the annual accounts, and update changes promptly through the applicable Commercial Registry or notarial reporting channel. Transfers of shares must also be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the beneficial ownership information where control changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder, if the SL is wholly owned by one shareholder
Beneficial Ownership information maintained through the applicable statutory registry and corporate records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300-1,000 annually, approximately USD 325-1,085. Spain does not generally require a registered agent; the range covers registered-office, corporate-secretarial, and filing-support services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately EUR 2,000-8,000, or USD 2,170-8,680, for a small or medium-sized SL, depending on turnover, transaction volume, group reporting, and audit complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly formed entities on taxable profits for the first two years (subject to conditions). Additional deductions for R&D activities, export promotion, and job creation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) electronic portal (www.agenciatributaria.es)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the 6 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for FY ending 31 December, deadline is 25 July of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Spanish NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) assigned to the non-resident entity. If not yet assigned, apply for one via Form 036 before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the fiscal year covered by the return. Must match the statutory accounting period.
Compute taxable income after adjustments for permanent and temporary differences. Non-residents with a permanent establishment in Spain must allocate income attributable to that PE.
Apply the standard 25% rate, or the reduced 15% rate if eligible as a newly created entity. Non-residents without a PE are subject to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) via Form 210, not Form 200.
Claim applicable double tax relief, R&D credits, or other incentives. Attach supporting documentation as required.
Calculate final liability after credits and prepayments. If a refund is due, provide bank details for transfer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 5% of the tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline; 10% if within 6 months; 15% if within 12 months; 20% if after 12 months. Surcharge of 1% per month of delay (capped at 20%). Interest on late payment accrues at the statutory rate (currently 3.75% per annum).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 202 (Quarterly Corporate Income Tax Prepayment) filed via AEAT electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 20 days after the end of each quarter (April 20, July 20, October 20, and December 20 for the fourth quarter).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same as Form 200; use the NIF assigned to the permanent establishment.
Calculate based on the cumulative taxable income for the year-to-date, applying the same adjustments as in the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayment rate (18% for general companies, 20% for those with net turnover > EUR 10 million)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the applicable rate. For new companies, the rate is 15% for the first two years.
Pay the calculated amount via direct debit or bank transfer. No offset against prior losses is allowed in prepayments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 5% of the amount due if filed within 3 months of deadline; 10% if within 6 months; 15% if within 12 months; 20% if after 12 months. Surcharge of 1% per month of delay (capped at 20%). Interest on late payment at 3.75% per annum.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must submit Form 210 (Non-Resident Income Tax Return) and provide a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the residence country. The TRC must be valid for the relevant fiscal year and include the beneficial ownership declaration. The payer must retain a copy of the TRC and the Form 210 for audit purposes. For EU/EEA residents, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) may eliminate withholding tax if the parent holds at least 5% of the subsidiary's capital for at least 12 months. The payer must verify the holding period and obtain a declaration from the parent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Statutory rate 24% (for non-residents without PE). Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC), the rate is 0% if the beneficial owner is an associated company of an EU member state (holding at least 25% for at least 24 months). Treaty rates vary (e.g., 5-10% for royalties, 5-10% for interest). Interest: Statutory rate 19% (for non-residents without PE). Treaty rates typically 5-10%. For EU associated companies, the Interest & Royalties Directive may reduce to 0% under conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 (total net turnover) for mandatory Master File and Local File. For entities below this threshold, Local File is required if related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 per counterparty or EUR 1,000,000 in aggregate. Simplified documentation is available for SMEs (turnover < EUR 10 million) with transactions below EUR 1 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime like the UAE, but general anti-abuse rules (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles apply. Companies must demonstrate real economic activity (e.g., employees, premises, decision-making) to avoid recharacterization of transactions or denial of treaty benefits. The Spanish Tax Agency may challenge entities lacking substance, especially in holding or financing structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false invoicing, or concealment of assets to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the evaded tax amount, plus interest. Criminal prosecution for amounts exceeding EUR 120,000 per year may result in imprisonment (1-5 years) and fines up to 6 times the evaded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for tax debts if they were involved in the evasion or failed to prevent it. Civil restitution, travel bans, and disqualification from holding directorships may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a mere conduit with no real business activity, no employees, no premises, or no actual decision-making in Spain, while claiming tax benefits or treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of a 19% withholding tax on deemed dividends. Penalties for non-compliance with substance requirements can reach EUR 10,000 per infraction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if the company is deemed a sham. They may face civil claims from creditors and tax authorities, and in severe cases, criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures (e.g., customer due diligence, record-keeping, reporting suspicious transactions) as required by Law 10/2010.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines from EUR 60,000 to EUR 5,000,000 depending on severity. For serious infractions, fines up to 10% of annual turnover. Criminal liability for money laundering may result in imprisonment (6 months to 6 years) and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML failures if they knowingly or negligently allowed the company to be used for money laundering. They may face criminal prosecution, travel bans, and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain adequate transfer pricing documentation, or applying non-arm's length prices in related-party transactions, leading to profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 15% on the adjusted amount (or 25% if the adjustment exceeds EUR 100,000). Interest on underpaid tax accrues. In cases of intentional non-compliance, penalties can be up to 50% of the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the company's tax debts if they signed the tax return knowing the transfer pricing was incorrect. Civil liability for damages to the company and shareholders may also arise.
